cards.text: Jesus has just told His disciples that this Scripture must be fulfilled in Him: 'And He was numbered with the transgressors' (Luke 22:37). Now He goes out, as usual, to the Mount of Olives. The disciples follow Him.

cards.question: When they reach the place on the Mount of Olives, Jesus tells the disciples what to pray for. What is it?

answers.text: That they will not enter into temptation
That the crowds will leave them alone
That the city will welcome their message

cards.text: Then Jesus goes on about a stone's throw beyond them and kneels down. He prays, "Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me."

cards.question: After asking the Father to take this cup from Him, Jesus prays for His own will to be done.
While Jesus is praying on the Mount of Olives, someone appears from heaven and strengthens Him. Who is it?

cards.text: Jesus is in anguish now, and He prays more earnestly. This isn't a quick prayer, friend. This is the hardest prayer anyone has ever prayed.

cards.question: As Jesus prays in His anguish, His sweat becomes like drops of blood falling to the ground.

cards.text: Jesus rises from prayer and goes back to the disciples. Now remember, before He walked off, He asked them to pray.

cards.question: When Jesus comes back from praying, what does He find the disciples doing?
Luke says the disciples fell asleep because they were exhausted from ___.

cards.text: "Why are you sleeping?" Jesus asks. Then that line again: "Get up and pray so that you will not enter into temptation."
While Jesus is still speaking, a crowd arrives. Leading it is the man called Judas, one of the Twelve.

cards.question: Judas walks right up to Jesus in front of the crowd. What is he coming to do?

cards.text: But Jesus asks him, "Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?" He knows exactly what this is.
The men around Jesus see what's about to happen. They ask, "Lord, should we strike with our swords?" Notice they ask first. Very polite. Hold that thought.

cards.question: Before Jesus answers, one of the men around Him swings his sword. Who does he hit?

answers.text: The servant of the high priest

cards.question: The sword cuts off the servant's ___ ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus answers: "No more of this!" So much for asking first, friend. I think he heard "should we" and his arm took it as a yes.

cards.question: Jesus touches the servant's ear and heals him.

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks to the chief priests, temple officers and elders who came for Him. They brought swords and clubs. For the Man who just healed their guy's ear.

cards.question: Jesus asks if they've come out with swords and clubs as they would against an ___.
Jesus tells the chief priests and elders that every day He was with them in the temple courts, they laid hands on Him.
Jesus tells the crowd that this hour belongs to them and to something else. What is it?

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now. Keep the oven warm, friend, because this story is far from over.

findings.problem: "This is the hardest prayer anyone has ever prayed" is a factual claim that the text doesn't make. Luke 22:44 says only that He prayed more earnestly in His anguish. A storyteller line can carry the moment, but it can't add a fact.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences. Only the opening card can be that long.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has no humor at all. Every story card reads like a plain retelling. Jesus' prayer must stay reverent, but the disciples falling asleep after being asked to pray (Luke 22:45) is a human moment that could hold a respectful laugh. Card 8 sets this up but never lands a joke.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The story card has 5 sentences: "The men around Jesus see what's about to happen. They ask, ... Notice they ask first. Very polite. Hold that thought."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "I think he heard 'should we' and his arm took it as a yes" gives a reason for the sword strike. Luke 22:50 gives none. A guess marked with "I think" is allowed for feelings, not for reasons. The joke is also muddled: the man who struck was one of "those around Jesus" who asked the question (Luke 22:49-50), so he didn't simply hear it.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "Then Jesus speaks to ... They brought swords and clubs. For the Man who just healed their guy's ear."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus speaks to "the crowd." Luke 22:52-53 says He is speaking to the chief priests, temple officers and elders who had come for Him. The crowd is what Luke 22:47 calls the group Judas led.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
